newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ionica says undercuts BT by 15-20 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ionica says undercuts BT by 15-20 pct.

text.p: Ionica, the fledgling UK telephone company based on wireless technology, pledged on Friday to peg its basic prices and discount schemes to at least 15 percent below those of its giant rival British Telecommunications (BT).
Ionica, which delivers its telecoms services via radio waves to antennae on houses, said customers would save 15 percent on all UK calls and virtually all international calls.
When compared with BT, customers would also pay 20 percent less for fixed charges such as line rental, it added.
"Even if a user takes all BT's discount schemes, Ionica will still be offering a service at least 15-20 percent less expensive," Ionica's chief executive Nigel Playford said in a statement.

Ionica, partly-owned by Yorkshire Electricity and Northern Electric, has a national licence and plans to extend its network from the east of England to cover three quarters of homes in England and Wales by 2000.

The group on Friday also launched its "Favourite Numbers" discount scheme, which like BT's "Friends and Family" scheme, gives customers an extra 10 percent saving on 10 selected numbers. But Ionica said these savings were on top of the 15 percent they already save against BT's standard rates.
